response.rationale: Both answers are semantically appropriate for “sweater.” Indonesian “sweter” is a standard form, while Malaysian Malay uses “baju panas” as a dictionary translation; “sweater” is also an established Malaysian Malay borrowing. The different-common-word relation is valid as a contrast of preferred forms, though not an absolute exclusivity claim. No false-friend contrast is present or required.
